title: Grade 2 Math — Tue, Jun 10
description: Measurement — Day 2 of 5: Comparing lengths; cm and m
subject: mathematics

questions.question: A ribbon is 80 cm long. Another ribbon is 1 m long. Which is longer?
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm. 100 cm > 80 cm, so the 1 m ribbon is longer.

questions.question: Aman is 120 cm tall. His sister is 1 m tall. Who is taller?
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm. 120 cm > 100 cm, so Aman is taller.

questions.question: A bed is 190 cm long. Is it longer or shorter than 2 m?
questions.explanation: 2 m = 200 cm. 190 cm < 200 cm, so the bed is shorter than 2 m.

questions.question: Which is shorter — 50 cm or half a metre?
questions.explanation: Half a metre = 50 cm. They are exactly the same length.

questions.question: A rope is 5 m long. How many cm is that?
Priya's table is 100 cm long. Raj's table is 1 m long. Whose table is longer?
options: Both tables are the same length
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm. Both tables are exactly the same length.

questions.question: A hallway is 4 m long. How long is that in cm?
A wall is 250 cm high. Is it more than 2 m or less than 2 m?
questions.explanation: 2 m = 200 cm. 250 cm > 200 cm, so the wall is more than 2 m.

questions.question: A pencil is 15 cm. A pen is 16 cm. Which is shorter?
questions.explanation: 15 cm < 16 cm. The pencil (15 cm) is shorter.

questions.question: How many 50 cm pieces can be cut from a 1 m rope?
Which is longer — 99 cm or 1 m?
questions.explanation: 1 m = 100 cm. 100 cm > 99 cm, so 1 m is longer.

questions.question: Meena jumped 150 cm. Tina jumped 2 m. Who jumped farther?
questions.explanation: 2 m = 200 cm. 200 cm > 150 cm, so Tina jumped farther.
